title: Root-Zone Sensing, Dryback and Irrigation Scheduling

content.overview: Irrigation timing should reflect how quickly the root zone and plant use water under the actual crop environment. Dryback can be useful as a trend, but no single percentage or pulse count is a universal target across substrates, container sizes, cultivars and crop stages.

vocabulary.definition: Volume of water per volume of substrate or soil, often estimated with calibrated sensors.
Decline in root-zone water content between irrigation events.
Delivery of the planned irrigation volume in multiple smaller events rather than one large event.

sections.title: Sensor trends need calibration and context
sections.body: Water-content sensor output depends on substrate and installation. Use trends with known wet/dry reference behavior rather than treating an unverified raw value as absolute truth.

sections.title: Plant demand changes through the day and crop cycle
sections.body: Transpiration-driven nutrient-uptake work in cannabis reinforces that water and nutrient use are dynamic. Light, VPD, plant size and stage influence demand.

sections.title: Schedule changes should be tested by root-zone response
sections.body: When crop size, media, container or environment changes, re-evaluate irrigation timing and volume instead of copying the prior schedule.

workedExamples: A young transplant in a large container may need a different wetting pattern than a fully rooted flowering plant in the same container.
Two rooms at the same clock schedule can have different dryback if PPFD, VPD or plant size differs.
commonMistakes: Using one dryback percentage for every substrate.
Assuming a moisture sensor is accurate in a new media without verification.
content.practicalApplication: Trend representative root-zone water content with irrigation timestamps, environment and plant stage, then adjust one scheduling variable at a time and observe the response.
content.summary: Advanced irrigation scheduling is feedback control built from root-zone trends and plant demand, not universal timing recipes.
